rule.old: An output is excluded from scoring for every model when its reference depends on an engine input that the certified household data never carried and the prompt therefore never listed, and a careful reader could take the stated facts the other way.
rule.new: An output is excluded from scoring for every model when its reference depends on an input or definition that the certified household data never carried and the prompt therefore never stated, and a careful reader could take the stated facts the other way.

derivation_insert.before: On 2026-09-29 the references moved to policyengine-us 2.15.17
derivation_insert.text: On 2026-10-05 eight more outputs were excluded on review of release dashboard-data-20260930 (reference_audit/2026-10-05, reference_audit/2026-10-05-medicare-part-b and reference_audit/2026-10-05-payroll); their records are computed on policyengine-us 2.15.17, whose values are the references, and each sweep's baseline reproduced every scored reference.

adjudications.reasoning: The frozen reference is 11,113.57; the alternative is 11,895.23. The prompt lists no state income tax withheld or paid during 2026; policyengine-us 2.15.17 fills the state income tax part of the federal state and local tax deduction with state_withheld_income_tax, a formula estimate of California withholding on federal AGI ($6,058.85), while read as the household paying its 2026 California income tax during the year the deduction takes the engine's liability ($2,505.87). Found in the 2026-10-05 audit of the state income tax in SALT (reference_audit/2026-10-05, scripts/sweep_salt_withholding.py).

The frozen reference is 2,346.10; the alternative is 2,218.50. The prompt counts mandatory employee state payroll taxes; Minnesota Paid Leave contributions are the employer's, which may deduct the employee share from wages but need not (Minn. Stat. 268B.14, subds. 1, 3 and 5a), and policyengine-us 2.15.17 counts the largest share the employer may deduct ($127.60); read as the amount the law requires of the employee, $0, the output is employee federal payroll tax alone. Found in the 2026-10-05 audit of state payroll components (reference_audit/2026-10-05-payroll, program_classification.json).

The frozen reference is 330.73; the alternative is 312.74. The prompt counts mandatory employee state payroll taxes; Colorado FAMLI contributions are the employer's, which may deduct the employee share from wages but need not (C.R.S. 8-13.3-507(2) and (5); 7 CCR 1107-1 s. 1.4(6)(A)), and policyengine-us 2.15.17 counts the largest share the employer may deduct ($17.99); read as the amount the law requires of the employee, $0, the output is employee federal payroll tax alone. Found in the 2026-10-05 audit of state payroll components (reference_audit/2026-10-05-payroll, program_classification.json).

Found in the 2026-10-05 audit of the state income tax in SALT (reference_audit/2026-10-05, scripts/sweep_salt_withholding.py).

The frozen reference is 10,729.61; the alternative is 11,137.31. The prompt lists no state income tax withheld or paid during 2026; policyengine-us 2.15.17 fills the state income tax part of the federal state and local tax deduction with state_withheld_income_tax, a formula estimate of Virginia withholding on federal AGI ($5,367.30), while read as the household paying its 2026 Virginia income tax during the year the deduction takes the engine's liability ($3,514.15). The reference's medical deduction also counts a modeled Medicare Part B premium ($2,434.80) the prompt does not list; without it the output is 11,265.27. Found in the 2026-10-05 audits of the state income tax in SALT (reference_audit/2026-10-05) and of the Part B premium (reference_audit/2026-10-05-medicare-part-b).

The frozen reference is 3,514.15; the alternative is 3,654.15. The prompt lists no Medicare enrollment or Part B premium; policyengine-us 2.15.17 treats the 69-year-old head as enrolled (takes_up_medicare_if_eligible defaults to true) and adds the $2,434.80 standard Part B premium to medical expenses, which Virginia's itemized deductions carry from the federal ones; read with no premium paid, the output is the alternative. Found in the 2026-10-05 audit of the Part B premium (reference_audit/2026-10-05-medicare-part-b, scripts/sweep_part_b.py).
